### Galiano Gold Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results


November 5, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s203.q4cdn.com/835664992/files/doc_news/Galiano-Gold-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Results-2026.pdf)


Gold Production Increases 19% Quarter over Quarter, Full-Year Guidance Remains on Track at the Asanko Gold Mine


Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 5, 2026) - **Galiano Gold Inc. (TSX: GAU) (NYSE American: GAU) ("Galiano" or the "Company")** is pleased to report its third quarter ("Q3") 2026 operating and financial results. Galiano's operating asset is its 90% interest in the Asanko Gold Mine ("AGM") located in the Republic of Ghana, West Africa.


"Our team delivered a strong third quarter producing 40,922 gold ounces, improving all-in sustaining costs and achieving positive operating cash flows of $57 million. These results reflect the strength of our operations and position us well to achieve our full-year 2026 production and cost guidance," said Matt Badylak, Galiano's President and Chief Executive Officer.


"The recent extension of key mining licenses combined with a robust balance sheet provides a solid foundation to continue investing in the long-term growth of the AGM. During the quarter, we advanced several strategic initiatives, including resource definition drilling at Esaase, activities supporting the future underground development of Abore and accelerated waste stripping at Nkran Cut 3. These investments are designed to enhance operational flexibility and unlock additional value across the mine plan. We remain firmly on track to deliver our updated mineral reserves and mineral resources estimates in the first quarter of 2027. With our hedge book set to expire by year-end, we anticipate a significant inflection point in cash flow generation in 2027, positioning the Company to create sustainable long-term value."


All financial information contained in this news release is unaudited and reported in United States dollars.


**Q3 2026 AND YEAR-TO-DATE HIGHLIGHTS**


**Safety**


- No lost-time injuries ("LTI") nor total recordable injuries (inclusive of LTIs) ("TRI") recorded during Q3 2026. The AGM has achieved 13.4 million hours worked without an LTI, equating to 548 accident-free days, as of September 30, 2026.


- 12‐month rolling LTI and TRI frequency rates as of September 30, 2026 of 0.00 and 0.00 per million hours worked, respectively.


**Financial**


- Cash and cash equivalents of $86.8 million and restricted cash of $25.9 million as of September 30, 2026 and no debt.


- Generated cash flow from operating activities of $57.0 million during Q3 2026.


- Income from mine operations of $72.2 million during Q3 2026.


- Net income of $0.15 and adjusted net income\[1\] of $0.09 per common share (basic) during Q3 2026.


- Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization ("EBITDA1") of $82.3 million and Adjusted EBITDA1 of $93.3 million during Q3 2026.


- Settled 22,500 ounces of gold hedges during Q3 2026. The Company has 15,000 ounces remaining under its hedging program that are expected to be settled in Q4 2026.


**Mining Operations**


- Mined 1.7 million tonnes ("Mt") of ore at an average mined grade of 1.0 grams per tonne ("g/t") gold with a strip ratio of 4.4:1 during Q3 2026. Approximately 82% of mined ore was from the Abore deposit.


**Processing**


- 1.4 Mt of ore was milled at an average feed grade of 1.0 g/t, with metallurgical recovery averaging 90% during Q3 2026. Mill availability during the quarter was 92%.


- Produced 40,922 ounces of gold during the quarter, 19% higher than Q2 2026, and 110,060 ounces of gold year-to-date.


- The Company maintains its full-year 2026 production guidance of between 140,000 ounces and 160,000 ounces of gold.


- Sold 40,403 ounces of gold during the quarter and 109,831 ounces of gold year-to-date at average prices of $4,247 per ounce ("/oz") and $4,497/oz, respectively, excluding the effect of realized losses on gold hedging instruments.


**Nkran Cut 3 Development**


- Development of Cut 3 at the Nkran deposit accelerated during the quarter with 8.5 Mt of waste mined, an increase of 40% from Q2 2026. Additional mining equipment was mobilized during Q3 2026, leading to increased mining rates at Nkran that are anticipated to further increase in Q4 2026.


- Capitalized development pre-stripping costs at Nkran Cut 3 of $24.6 million during Q3 2026 and $60.2 million year-to-date.


**Costs**


- All-in sustaining costs1 ("AISC") of $2,346/oz for the quarter, a 5% decrease compared to Q2 2026 primarily resulting from higher gold ounces sold.


- Year-to-date AISC1 of $2,391/oz. The Company maintains its full-year 2026 AISC1 guidance of between $2,300/oz and $2,600/oz.


**Mining Lease Extension**


- The Abirem and Miradani mining leases were extended by 15 years and 17 years through 2041 and 2043, respectively. The leases host the Nkran, Adubiaso, and Miradani North deposits, as well as the AGM's processing facility. Securing these mining lease extensions lays the foundation for operational certainty and production growth at the AGM.


**Exploration**


- The Esaase conversion drilling program was completed during Q3 2026 with approximately 32,900 meters ("m") for the program. Data review and modelling are underway, and results of this work are expected to be included in the AGM's 2027 mineral reserves and mineral resources update planned for Q1 2027.


- During the quarter, approximately 4,500m were drilled at Abore and year-to-date drilling stands at approximately 20,600m of a planned 32,000m program. The objective of this program is to test extensions of mineralization 200m below Abore's existing underground mineral resource.


- Secured the necessary regulatory approvals in Ghana to develop an underground exploration adit at the Abore deposit. The Company has commenced a contract tender and mining contractor selection process.

**Q3 2026 Operational Analysis for the Asanko Gold Mine**


**Mining**


- Mined 1.4 Mt of ore at the Abore deposit at an average grade of 1.1 g/t gold and a strip ratio of 3.4:1. Mined grades at Abore during Q3 2026 increased by 9% compared to Q2 2026, as higher grades at deeper elevations began to be mined.


- Mined 0.3 Mt of ore at the Esaase deposit at an average grade of 0.8 g/t gold and a strip ratio of 10.9:1. Mined ore tonnes and grade were largely consistent with Q2 2026.


- Mining costs per tonne at Abore and Esaase averaged $4.53 per tonne ("/t") in Q3 2026, consistent with Q2 2026.


**Processing**


- The AGM produced 40,922 ounces of gold during Q3 2026, a 19% increase from Q2 2026 gold production, as the processing plant milled 1.4 Mt of ore at an average grade of 1.0 g/t gold with metallurgical recovery averaging 90%.


- Mill throughput in Q3 2026 was 11% higher than Q2 2026 as there was less plant downtime in the current quarter. Consequently, mill availability improved from 90% in Q2 2026 to 92% during Q3 2026.


- Approximately 80% of the mill feed was sourced from mined ore at Abore, with the remainder of mill feed primarily from the Esaase deposit.


- Processing costs per tonne for Q3 2026 was $15.40, a 10% increase from Q2 2026. The increase in processing costs per tonne was largely driven by replacement of mill liners and maintenance on the primary crusher and ball mill.


**Costs**


- AISC1 for Q3 2026 was $2,346/oz, compared to $2,473/oz in Q2 2026. The 5% decrease in AlSC1 resulted from more gold ounces sold, partly offset by higher sustaining capital expenditures related to a tailings facility expansion.


- For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, reported AISC1 was $2,391/oz, tracking in line with full-year 2026 cost guidance of between $2,300/oz and $2,600/oz.


**Nkran Cut 3**


- Nkran Cut 3 waste stripping accelerated during the quarter with 8.5 Mt of waste rock mined, an increase of 40% from Q2 2026, which was supported by the mobilization of additional mining equipment.


- Mining costs per tonne at Nkran was $2.87 for Q3 2026, compared to $3.58/t in Q2 2026. The decrease in mining unit costs was driven by higher tonnes mined.


- Nkran Cut 3 development capitalized stripping costs totaled $24.6 million during Q3 2026 and $60.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.


**Capital Expenditures**


- Sustaining capital expenditures totaled $5.0 million during Q3 2026, $3.0 million higher than Q2 2026. The increase in sustaining capital expenditures in Q3 2026 related to advancing the construction of a tailings facility expansion.


- Development capital expenditures during Q3 2026 totaled $2.2 million, consistent with Q2 2026. Development capital expenditures in Q3 2026 related mainly to costs of relocating villages near the AGM's operations.


**Exploration**


- An infill drilling program at Esaase was completed during Q3 2026. This program was designed to convert existing open pit mineral resources from the inferred to indicated category and has the potential to significantly increase Esaase's mineral reserves to support planning of potential open pit expansions. 16,732m of drilling was completed in the quarter, bringing the program total to approximately 32,900m. Data review and modelling are underway, and results of this work are expected to be included in the AGM's 2027 mineral reserves and mineral resources update planned for Q1 2027.


- A drilling program at Abore, designed to expand the underground mineral resource through step out drilling to at least 200m below the maiden underground mineral resource, resumed in late Q3 2026. The Abore drilling campaign was previously paused to prioritize the Esaase conversion drilling program. During the quarter, 4,445m were drilled at Abore and year-to-date drilling stands at approximately 20,600m of a planned 32,000m program. Completion of this underground drilling program is expected in Q4 2026.

**1** **Non-IFRS Performance Measures**


The Company has included certain non-IFRS performance measures in this news release. These non-IFRS performance measures do not have any standardized meaning and therefore may not be comparable to similar measures presented by other issuers. Accordingly, these performance measures are intended to provide additional information and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for measures of performance prepared in accordance with IFRS accounting standards. Refer to *"Non-IFRS Measures"* of Galiano's Management's Discussion and Analysis for an explanation of these measures and reconciliations to the Company's reported financial results in accordance with IFRS accounting standards.


- **Total Cash Costs per Gold Ounce Sold** Management of the Company uses total cash costs per gold ounce sold to monitor the operating performance of the AGM. Total cash costs include the costs of gold production, adjusted for costs allocated to by-products and production royalties per ounce of gold sold.


- **AISC per Gold Ounce Sold** The Company has adopted the reporting of "AISC per gold ounce sold". AISC includes total cash costs, AGM general and administrative expenses, sustaining capital expenditure, sustaining capitalized stripping costs, reclamation cost accretion and lease payments made on the AGM's mining and other service lease agreements per ounce of gold sold.


- **EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA** EBITDA provides an indication of the Company's continuing capacity to generate income from operations before taking into account the Company's financing decisions and costs of amortizing capital assets. Accordingly, EBITDA comprises net income (loss) excluding finance expense, finance income, depreciation and depletion expense, and income taxes. Adjusted EBITDA adjusts EBITDA to exclude non-recurring items and non-cash items ("Adjusted EBITDA").


- **Adjusted Net Income (Loss) and Adjusted Net Income (Loss) per Common Share** The Company has included the non-IFRS performance measures of adjusted net income (loss) and adjusted net income (loss) per common share. Neither adjusted net income (loss) nor adjusted net income (loss) per share have any standardized meaning and are therefore unlikely to be comparable to other measures presented by other issuers. Adjusted net income (loss) excludes certain non-cash items, and items of income or expense not expected to recur in the future, from net income (loss) to provide a measure which helps the Company and investors to evaluate the results of the underlying core operations of the Company and its ability to generate cash flows and is an important indicator of the strength of the Company's operations and performance of its core business.
